jobs.text: Silkworms feed on mulberry leaves and spin cocoons, and the threads are boiled and reeled into yarn. Rajshahi silk has been famous since the Mughal period and was once widely exported. The industry shrank in the late twentieth century, and it is now being revived by weavers and government programmes.

jobs.text: Somapura Mahavihara was built by Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty in the late eighth century and was one of the largest Buddhist monasteries south of the Himalayas. A vast square courtyard is lined with 177 cells for monks, and terracotta plaques around the central temple show scenes of everyday village life. UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 1985.
